title: SmartRouter: disentangle policy engine, normalize fallback chains, and regional routing cleanup
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background: The SmartRouter service currently mixes policy evaluation, region capability checks, and fallback selection in a single monolithic path. This results in high cognitive overhead, duplicated logic across handlers, synchronous DB/etcd reads on the hot path, and brittle fallback semantics that are hard to test and reason about.

Goals:
- Extract a small, composable policy evaluation engine (policy evaluators + pipeline) that is deterministic and unit-testable.
- Replace implicit fallback heuristics with an explicit, declarative fallback chain DSL that is versioned per model route.
- Centralize regional capability and model-variant metadata into a TTL-cached capability map to remove blocking I/O from request flow.
- Reduce p95/p99 routing latency by eliminating 1-2 synchronous network calls per request and by simplifying hot-path branching.
- Add comprehensive unit/integration tests and observable metrics (policy decisions, fallback step counts, cache hit/miss rates).

Scope: Router service (smart-routing component), policy evaluation library, and capability cache. Does NOT include API surface changes or frontend Console UX. Does NOT change customer-facing routing policies; the refactor is behaviour-preserving by default.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy engine implemented with >90% unit test coverage for evaluators used in production.
- Declarative fallback chain applied to a test route; behaviour matches legacy logic in canary (no regressions).
- Routing latency improvement: remove at least one synchronous capability DB roundtrip in hot path and decrease median router processing time by >=5ms on our internal latency dataset.
- Monitoring: dashboards for fallback usage, policy eval failures, capability map cache hit rate, and rollout canary metrics.
- Rollout plan with feature flag and progressive enabling by region.

Non-goals: Rewriting the entire routing stack, modifying model matching semantics, or changing SLA guarantees as part of this ticket.
comments: 2025-11-07 - Kickoff: Align with Platform and Runtime teams. Decided to keep behaviour identical during canary; new DSL will compile to same fallback sequence as today unless a route opts-in to newer policies.

2025-11-10 - Design: Chose evaluator pipeline pattern (chain of responsibility with pure functions) over rules-engine dependency to keep code footprint small and avoid dynamic rule compilation in hot path.

2025-11-14 - Trade-offs: We discussed strong consistency for capability map but chose eventual consistency with 15s TTL to avoid p95 spikes; fallback semantics will prefer same-region with degraded variants instead of immediate cross-region routing during short staleness windows.
2025-11-18 - PR DRAFT: Initial policy evaluator interfaces and in-memory capability map. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/341 (WIP).

2025-11-20 - Review feedback from @li-chen: tighten interface surface, remove context.Context usage in evaluator signatures to keep them pure; add explicit error types for 'unavailable' vs 'policy-deny'.

2025-11-25 - Performance note: Microbenchmarks show evaluator pipeline adds ~0.8us per check; bulk savings from removing two etcd calls equates to ~6-10ms median improvement in staging synthetic workload.

2025-11-29 - Integration: Added a compatibility shim layer that translates the new fallback DSL to the legacy runtime fallback invocations so we can run a canary without changing route config. Integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/357

2025-12-01 - QA: End-to-end tests created that run the old and new routing paths against the same request corpus and assert identical selected endpoints for >99.9% of cases (exceptions documented as known out-of-scope mismatches). Test artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abc-routing-tests

2025-12-02 - Plan for rollout: feature flag 'smartrouter.policy.v2' with phased rollout by region (us-west-2 -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1). Monitor fallback counts, 5xxs, and p95 latency; automatic rollback if 5xxs spike >1.5x baseline or fallback usage increases >3x.
Follow-ups: Add a small operator endpoint to invalidate capability cache per-region in case of emergency for faster recovery; schedule as separate ticket if needed (ENG-7210 suggested).
